text:
**Short answer:** for most 16-year-olds, the **Starling Teen account** or the **Monzo 16–17 account** is the best first account. If you want to earn interest, look at **Nationwide FlexOne**. Details change, so check each bank's own page before applying.

**Best overall (app-based): Starling Teen or Monzo 16–17**
- Starling's Teen account is designed specifically for 16 and 17 year olds. Finder gives it its top score, and Which? lists it as a recommended provider with an 86% customer score.
- Monzo's 16–17 account is also free, and you can open it entirely on your own. Which? gives it 85%.
- Both are fee-free, and Starling and Monzo both offer fee-free spending abroad. They also have savings pots and budgeting tools.
- Both are app-only, so there are no branches.

**Best if you want interest: Nationwide FlexOne**
- It's open to 11–17s and has a free Visa debit card. It pays 2% AER on balances up to £1,000, and the linked FlexOne Saver pays 5.00% AER (variable) on up to £5,000. Rates change, so check them.
- A November 2026 guide says Nationwide FlexOne and HSBC MyMoney pay the most interest among the accounts it compared.

**Best if you want a high-street bank with branches: Lloyds, NatWest, Barclays or Santander**
- Monzo, Starling, NatWest Adapt, Lloyds Under 19s and Santander 123 Mini can all be opened by a 16- or 17-year-old alone, with photo ID and proof of address.
- Which? lists NatWest Adapt at 2.05% and Santander 123 Mini at 3% interest. Those figures come from an older review, so they may have changed.
- Barclays' Young Person's Account has a 2.99% fee for spending abroad, so it's less good for travel.

**Things to know**
- Monzo 16-17, Starling, NatWest Adapt, Lloyds Under 19s, Barclays, TSB Under 19s, Santander 123 Mini, HSBC MyMoney and Nationwide FlexOne all have no monthly fee. You shouldn't need to pay for a basic account.
- These are real, regulated accounts, so the money is protected by the FSCS up to £120,000.
- You'll normally need photo ID (a passport is easiest) and proof of address.
- Don't pay for a prepaid card or subscription app like GoHenry unless you want its parental controls. A free account does the same job for a 16-year-old.

**My suggestion:** open Starling or Monzo as your main spending account. If you have savings, you could also open a Nationwide FlexOne for the interest. Many people use more than one. Overdrafts usually aren't available until 18.

I can narrow this down if you tell me what matters most to you, such as interest, travel, branches or parental visibility.
